details: A recheck exists to land a branch on the newest master; one that runs on a branch behind master proves nothing the landing needs (principle 2: waste built into the setup).
failing_case: cycle.js with a recheck unit on a branch whose merge-base with master is not master's head gates and checks it and reports ready.
pass_cases: A recheck unit first takes the base branch with a merge commit (or stops and says the branch is behind) before its gate.
A recheck on a branch that already contains master's head runs as today.
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py test_recheck_gate_takes_the_base_first_and_a_conflict_stops_without_a_fix_round (line ~198) passes at head and fails at 336b5442 (AssertionError line 205).
findings.summary: A recheck runs on a branch that has not taken master

details: CONFIRMED by reading: cycle.js line 16 was updated, the skill text that the front reads to choose and prepare units
was not (git grep -n -i recheck lists SKILL.md:118 and front SKILL.md:126; neither was touched by the change).
The take is a no-op on a branch already holding master, so nothing breaks, but the front's routine take stays,
which is waste on every landing: MEDIUM by principle 2. Touching a skill text joins the next paid run on master
(no run per change). Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: git diff --stat master...HEAD: only cycle.js, tests/test_cycle_workflow.py and the gate log changed.
git grep -n -i recheck: plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:118 "`recheck` (a branch that took the default branch, or"
failing_case: The front lands a branch behind master. It reads SKILL.md:118 "`recheck` (a branch that took the default branch, ...)"
and, as before, first sends a runner to merge master, then starts the recheck unit, whose gate runner merges again
("Already up to date"). One extra agent per landing, the waste the queue item was taken to remove. When the
recheck stops with stopped_at "gate" and first_fail "take conflict: a.py", nothing in the skill says this is a
take conflict for a fixer (front SKILL.md:126 path), not a red gate.
fix_hint: Rewrite SKILL.md:118-119 to: "`recheck` (a branch or a train with `items`; its gate runner first merges the default
branch, and a conflict stops it with "take conflict: <files>" for a fixer)".
pass_cases: 1. plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md describes recheck as: takes the default branch itself (merge commit) before its gate; no separate take is needed first.
2. The same text says a conflict on that take stops the unit at gate with first_fail "take conflict: <files>", and the front sends a fixer to resolve it, then a new recheck.
3. The cycle.js header line 16 ("take the base, gate, then the check(s), show") stays as it is.
reason: plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:118-121 says the recheck gate runner merges the base itself, no separate take, and a conflict stops at gate with "take conflict: <files>" for a fixer then a new recheck; cycle.js header untouched.
findings.summary: principle 2: the delegate skill still describes a recheck as a branch that already took the default branch, so the front keeps a separate take before every recheck, and the new take-conflict stop is not described
